questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
If you know the answer, please ________ your hand.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) raise
Why: "Raise" means to lift something; it takes an object ("your hand").
Why not the others: (A) "Rise" means to go up by itself and takes no object. (C) means to come into being. (D) is the past of "rise".
Key point: You raise something; the sun rises.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to VIGOROUS:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Energetic
Why: Vigorous means strong, healthy and full of energy.
Why not the others: (B) means unclear. (C) is close to the opposite. (D) is unrelated.
Key point: Vigorous exercise makes you breathe hard.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
I will finish the work tonight ________ I have to stay up late.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) even if
Why: "Even if" means "whether or not": staying up late will not stop him.
Why not the others: (A) reverses the sense. (C) shows purpose. (D) gives a reason that makes no sense.
Key point: Even if = whatever happens.

questions.question: Choose the one word for: "A person who always expects the worst to happen"
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Pessimist
Why: A pessimist expects the worst.
Why not the others: (A) expects the best. (C) sees things as they are. (D) believes that events are fixed by fate.
Key point: Pessimist and optimist are opposites.

questions.question:
Match the phrasal verbs in List-I with their meanings in List-II:

List-I
(A) Pick up
(B) Pick out
(C) Pick on
(D) Pick at

List-II
(I) Choose from a group
(II) Eat only small amounts without interest
(III) Learn without formal study
(IV) Keep criticising or bullying someone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: She picked up Tamil while living in Chennai — learnt informally (III); pick out a shirt — choose (I); the older boys pick on him — bully (IV); he picked at his food — ate little (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the first two; (B) swaps pick out and pick on; (C) swaps the last two.
Key point: The particle changes the meaning of "pick".

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:
A. As it rises, this vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets, forming clouds.
B. When the drops become too heavy for the air to hold, they fall as rain.
C. The sun heats the water in seas, rivers and lakes, turning some of it into vapour.
D. Inside the clouds, these droplets join together to form larger drops.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) C, A, D, B
Why: C introduces evaporation; A follows with "this vapour" forming clouds; D says "Inside the clouds, these droplets" join; B ends with the rain.
Why not the others: (A) mentions "the clouds" and "these droplets" before they form. (B) begins with "this vapour". (D) brings the rain before the drops join.
Key point: "This vapour" and "these droplets" link the steps.

questions.question:
Match the figures of speech in List-I with the examples in List-II:

List-I
(A) Euphemism
(B) Hyperbole
(C) Anaphora
(D) Oxymoron

List-II
(I) We shall not stop, we shall not rest, we shall not give up.
(II) The old man is no longer with us.
(III) It was an open secret that he wanted the job.
(IV) My father will kill me when he sees my marks.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: "No longer with us" gently means "has died" — euphemism (II); "will kill me" exaggerates — hyperbole (IV); "we shall not" repeated at the start of each phrase — anaphora (I); "open secret" — oxymoron (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps euphemism and hyperbole; (B) swaps hyperbole and anaphora; (D) swaps the last two.
Key point: A euphemism softens; a hyperbole exaggerates.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
Can you ________ the birds singing outside the window?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) hear
Why: After "Can you", the base form of a verb is needed; "hear" means to perceive sound.
Why not the others: (A) means in this place. (B) is a past form and cannot follow "can". (C) is an animal like a rabbit.
Key point: You hear with your ear.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
After two hours of study, you should ________ a short break.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) take
Why: The fixed collocation is "take a break".
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) do not go with "a break" in this sense.
Key point: Take a break, take a rest, take a nap.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
Lack of sleep had made him so ________ that he snapped at everyone over the smallest thing.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) irritable
Why: "Irritable" means easily annoyed or made angry, which fits snapping at everyone.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) contradict snapping at people.
Key point: The action in the sentence decides the word.

questions.sub_topic: The road that leads to the temple
questions.question:
Rearrange the following parts to form a meaningful sentence:
A. is very steep
B. to the hill temple
C. and narrow in places
D. The road that leads
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) D, B, A, C
Why: "The road that leads (D) to the hill temple (B) is very steep (A) and narrow in places (C)."
Why not the others: (A) separates "leads" from "to the hill temple". (B) starts with a lower-case part. (C) puts "and narrow" before "steep".
Key point: "Leads" needs its "to" phrase.

questions.question:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:

List-I
(A) Brisk
(B) Frail
(C) Sombre
(D) Shrewd

List-II
(I) Dark, serious or sad
(II) Weak and delicate
(III) Clever in judging situations, especially for one's own advantage
(IV) Quick and energetic
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: Brisk — quick and lively, as in a brisk walk (IV); frail — weak (II); sombre — dark and serious (I); shrewd — sharp in judgement (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps brisk and frail; (C) swaps frail and sombre; (D) swaps the last two.
Key point: A sombre mood is serious; a shrewd trader is sharp.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
A judge must be ________; he should gain nothing from the outcome of a case.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) disinterested
Why: "Disinterested" means impartial, having no personal advantage in a matter.
Why not the others: (B) means not interested or bored — a judge should be interested in the case. (C) means arousing interest. (D) is not a standard word.
Key point: A disinterested judge is fair; an uninterested one is bored.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
The lake was so ________ that it reflected the mountains like a mirror.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) tranquil
Why: "Tranquil" means calm and still, which explains the mirror-like reflection.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) describe rough water. (C) would not reflect clearly.
Key point: Only still water reflects like a mirror.

questions.question:
Choose the word most similar in meaning to the word in capitals:
The garden was SERENE in the evening light.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Peaceful
Why: Serene means calm and peaceful.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are close to opposites. (D) describes appearance, not calm.
Key point: A serene face shows no worry.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Sentence Transformation and Correctness
questions.question:
Choose the option that best expresses the sentence in indirect speech:
He said to me, "Thank you for your help."
options: A) He thanked me for my help.
B) He said me thank you for my help.
C) He told me that thank you for your help.
D) He thanked to me for your help.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) He thanked me for my help.
Why: "Thank you" is reported with the verb "thanked"; "your" becomes "my".
Why not the others: (B) and (C) keep the direct words in a broken structure. (D) adds "to" and keeps "your".
Key point: Greetings and thanks are reported with a verb such as thanked, wished or greeted.

questions.question:
Rearrange the following parts to complete the sentence that begins: "Before the race, the coach told us"
A. not to start
B. to warm up properly
C. and
D. too fast
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) B, C, A, D
Why: "Before the race, the coach told us to warm up properly (B) and (C) not to start (A) too fast (D)." "And" joins the two instructions, and "too fast" completes "not to start".
Why not the others: (A) separates "not to start" from "too fast" with "and". (C) begins with "and". (D) gives "and too fast not to start".
Key point: "And" joins two items of the same kind: to + verb, and not to + verb.

questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to RELAXED:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Tense
Why: Relaxed means free from tension; tense means stretched tight or nervous.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are close in meaning. (C) is unrelated.
Key point: Relaxed muscles are loose; tense muscles are tight.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
________ you have finished the test, hand your paper to the invigilator.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Once
Why: "Once" as a conjunction means "as soon as" or "after".
Why not the others: (A) gives a condition that reverses the sense. (B) shows contrast. (C) shows a precaution.
Key point: Once = as soon as.

questions.question:
Choose the word most opposite in meaning to the word in capitals:
Her ANCESTORS came to Kolkata from a village in Bihar.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Descendants
Why: Ancestors are those from whom one is descended; descendants are those who descend from a person.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) are unrelated in meaning. (D) is a synonym.
Key point: Ancestors come before; descendants come after.

questions.question:
Match the words in List-I with their definitions in List-II:

List-I
(A) Verbatim
(B) Unanimous
(C) Simultaneous
(D) Spontaneous

List-II
(I) In exactly the same words
(II) Agreed by everyone
(III) Happening at the same time
(IV) Done naturally, without planning
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
Why: Verbatim — word for word (I); unanimous — agreed by all (II); simultaneous — at the same time (III); spontaneous — unplanned (IV).
Why not the others: (B) swaps the first two; (C) swaps the middle two; (D) swaps the last two.
Key point: "Unanimous" comes from "one mind".

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Sentence Transformation and Correctness
questions.sub_topic: Correct sentences: since morning, one of the best, last year, too good
questions.question:
Which of the following sentences are grammatically correct?
A. The children are playing in the park since morning.
B. He is one of the best students in the class.
C. I have been to Shimla last year.
D. The news was too good to be true.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) B and D only
Why: B correctly uses "one of the best" + plural noun. D correctly uses "too ... to".
Why not the others: A should be "have been playing ... since morning". C should be "I went to Shimla last year". Options (A), (B) and (D) include A or C.
Key point: Actions continuing from a past point use the present perfect continuous.

questions.question:
Select the words that mean "to make someone calm or less angry":
A. pacify
B. provoke
C. soothe
D. specify
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and C only
D) A, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A and C only
Why: "Pacify" and "soothe" both mean to calm someone.
Why not the others: B (provoke) means to make angry — the opposite. D (specify) means to state exactly. Options (B), (C) and (D) include one of them.
Key point: Pacify is related to peace.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
The old man was sitting ________ in his armchair.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) comfortably
Why: The word describes how he "was sitting", so an adverb is needed.
Why not the others: (A) is a noun or verb. (B) is an adjective. (C) means giving comfort to others.
Key point: Adverbs describe verbs.

questions.sub_topic: Idioms: extra mile, break the bank, in two minds, get the hang of
questions.question:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:

List-I
(A) To go the extra mile
(B) To break the bank
(C) To be in two minds
(D) To get the hang of

List-II
(I) To cost more than one can afford
(II) To learn how to do something
(III) To make more effort than is expected
(IV) To be unable to decide
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: Go the extra mile — do more than expected (III); break the bank — cost too much (I); be in two minds — be undecided (IV); get the hang of — learn how to do (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the first two; (C) swaps the middle two; (D) swaps the last two.
Key point: Learn idioms as whole units of meaning.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to EXACERBATE:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Worsen
Why: Exacerbate means to make a problem, pain or feeling worse.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) only look similar. (D) is the opposite.
Key point: Scratching can exacerbate an itch.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank:
The teacher asked the excited children to ________ before the test began.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) calm down
Why: "Calm down" means to become quiet and relaxed.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not English phrasal verbs.
Key point: Calm down, settle down, quieten down.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank:
Read the instructions carefully at the ________ of the test.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) beginning
Why: The correct spelling doubles the "n": begin + n + ing = beginning.
Why not the others: (A) has one "n". (C) doubles the "g". (D) misses the second "n" before "-ing".
Key point: Begin doubles its final "n" before "-ing".

questions.sub_topic: Antonym pairs: presence, external, weary, praise
questions.question:
Select the correct pairs of antonyms:
A. presence — absence
B. external — internal
C. weary — tired
D. praise — criticise
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B, C and D
C) A, B and D only
D) B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A, B and D only
Why: Presence and absence, external and internal, praise and criticise are opposites.
Why not the others: Pair C is a pair of synonyms — weary means tired. Options (A), (B) and (D) include pair C.
Key point: Test each pair on its own.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
The long wait for the results caused her great ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) anxiety
Why: After "great", a noun is needed: "great anxiety".
Why not the others: (A) is an adjective. (B) is an adverb. (D) is not a correct form.
Key point: Anxious (adjective), anxiety (noun).

questions.question:
Rearrange the following parts to form a meaningful sentence:
A. Little did they know
B. would change their lives
C. that the small shop
D. they opened that summer
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A, C, D, B
Why: "Little did they know (A) that the small shop (C) they opened that summer (D) would change their lives (B)." The clause "they opened that summer" describes the shop.
Why not the others: (B) puts the verb before its subject. (C) starts with a lower-case part. (D) gives "the small shop would change their lives they opened that summer".
Key point: Little did + subject + know ... is an inverted negative.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the correct preposition to fill in the blank:
Careless driving can result ________ serious accidents.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) in
Why: "Result in" means to cause or lead to.
Why not the others: (A) "Result from" means to be caused by, which reverses the meaning. (B) and (D) are not standard.
Key point: Cause results in effect; effect results from cause.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Choosing the Correct Word
questions.question:
Choose the correct preposition to fill in the blank:
Parents are often worried ________ their children's health.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) about
Why: The standard expression is "worried about".
Why not the others: (B) is not English. (C) and (D) are not used with "worried".
Key point: Worried about, anxious about, concerned about.

questions.question:
Rearrange the following parts to form a meaningful sentence:
A. return their books
B. by the end of the month
C. All students must
D. to the library
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) C, A, D, B
Why: The opener with the subject and modal (C) is followed by the verb and object (A), where (D) and when (B).
Why not the others: (A) puts "to the library" before the verb. (B) and (D) start with a lower-case part.
Key point: Subject, verb, object, then place and time.

questions.topic: Verbal Ability: Sentence Transformation and Correctness
questions.question:
Choose the option that best expresses the sentence in the passive voice:
Many people speak English in India.
options: A) English was spoken by many people in India.
B) English is being spoken by many people in India.
C) English has been spoken by many people in India.
D) English is spoken by many people in India.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) English is spoken by many people in India.
Why: The simple present "speak" becomes "is spoken".
Why not the others: (A) is in the past. (B) is in the present continuous. (C) is in the present perfect.
Key point: Keep the tense when changing the voice.

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Imagine walking into an examination hall and seeing a question you cannot answer. Your heart pounds, your palms grow damp and your mouth goes dry. These feelings are not signs that something has gone wrong with your body. They are signs that it is working exactly as it was designed to.

When the brain senses a threat, a small region at its base, the hypothalamus, sends signals that cause the adrenal glands, which sit on top of the kidneys, to release hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol. Within seconds the heart beats faster, breathing quickens, muscles tighten and stored sugar pours into the blood to supply extra energy. Processes that are not urgent, such as digestion, slow down. Scientists call this the "fight-or-flight" response, because it prepared our distant ancestors either to fight a predator or to run from it.

In short bursts, this response can be useful. A little stress sharpens attention and can help an athlete run faster or a student think more quickly. The trouble begins when stress does not switch off. If a person feels under pressure for weeks or months, the body stays on alert, and the constant flow of stress hormones can disturb sleep, weaken the body's defences against illness and raise blood pressure.

The good news is that the body also has a way of calming itself, and we can help it. Regular exercise uses up stress hormones; slow, deep breathing signals to the brain that the danger has passed; enough sleep restores balance; and talking to a friend or family member makes problems feel lighter. None of these will remove every worry, but together they can stop ordinary stress from turning into a constant weight.

Question: According to the passage, where are the adrenal glands located?
options: A) At the base of the brain
D) On top of the kidneys
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) On top of the kidneys
Why: The passage refers to "the adrenal glands, which sit on top of the kidneys".
Why not the others: (A) is where the hypothalamus is. (B) and (C) are not stated.
Key point: Keep track of which organ is placed where.

Question: Why, according to the passage, does digestion slow down during the stress response?
options: A) It is not urgent when the body faces a threat
B) The stomach is damaged by adrenaline
C) The person has eaten too much before the examination
D) Cortisol stops all the body's organs from working
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) It is not urgent when the body faces a threat
Why: "Processes that are not urgent, such as digestion, slow down" while energy goes to fighting or running.
Why not the others: (B) and (D) are not stated; (D) exaggerates. (C) is unrelated.
Key point: Look for the reason the passage itself gives.

Question: Why is the stress response called "fight-or-flight"?
options: A) Because it makes people want to travel by air
B) It readied early humans to fight danger or flee it
C) Because it occurs only during quarrels with others
D) Because athletes always feel it just before a race
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) It readied early humans to fight danger or flee it
Why: "It prepared our distant ancestors either to fight a predator or to run from it." "Flight" here means running away.
Why not the others: (A) takes "flight" literally as air travel. (C) and (D) are not the reason for the name.
Key point: "Flight" can mean fleeing as well as flying.

Question: According to the passage, when does stress become harmful?
options: A) Whenever a person's heart beats faster
B) When the response stays switched on for a long time
C) When a student sees a hard question in an examination
D) When a person exercises too much
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) When the response stays switched on for a long time
Why: "The trouble begins when stress does not switch off. If a person feels under pressure for weeks or months ... stress hormones can disturb sleep, weaken the body's defences ... and raise blood pressure."
Why not the others: (A) and (C) describe the normal, short response. (D) Exercise is recommended.
Key point: Distinguish the short, useful response from the long, harmful one.

Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Imagine walking into an examination hall and seeing a question you cannot answer. Your heart pounds, your palms grow damp and your mouth goes dry. These feelings are not signs that something has gone wrong with your body. They are signs that it is working exactly as it was designed to.

When the brain senses a threat, a small region at its base, the hypothalamus, sends signals that cause the adrenal glands, which sit on top of the kidneys, to release hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol. Within seconds the heart beats faster, breathing quickens, muscles tighten and stored sugar pours into the blood to supply extra energy. Processes that are not urgent, such as digestion, slow down. Scientists call this the "fight-or-flight" response, because it prepared our distant ancestors either to fight a predator or to run from it.

In short bursts, this response can be useful. A little stress sharpens attention and can help an athlete run faster or a student think more quickly. The trouble begins when stress does not switch off. If a person feels under pressure for weeks or months, the body stays on alert, and the constant flow of stress hormones can disturb sleep, weaken the body's defences against illness and raise blood pressure.

The good news is that the body also has a way of calming itself, and we can help it. Regular exercise uses up stress hormones; slow, deep breathing signals to the brain that the danger has passed; enough sleep restores balance; and talking to a friend or family member makes problems feel lighter. None of these will remove every worry, but together they can stop ordinary stress from turning into a constant weight.

Question: Which of the following best states the writer's message?
options: A) All stress is dangerous and must be avoided
B) Students should never feel nervous in examinations
C) Stress hormones should be removed from the body by medicine
D) Stress is a natural response that we can learn to manage
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Stress is a natural response that we can learn to manage
Why: The writer explains that the response is natural and useful in short bursts, and ends with simple ways to help the body calm itself.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) contradict the passage. (C) No medicine is suggested.
Key point: A balanced passage needs a balanced answer.

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

The smartphone arrived in a cardboard box from Pune, sent by Arvind to his parents in the village, with a note in capital letters: "NOW WE CAN SEE EACH OTHER EVERY SUNDAY."

His father, Shankar Rao, who had driven a bus for thirty years, looked at the shining black slab as if it were a snake. "I have a phone," he said, pointing to the old handset with its rubber buttons. "It rings. I answer. What more is needed?"

His wife, Kamala, said nothing, but she kept the box on the shelf beside the gods.

It was their granddaughter Pinky, aged nine, who took charge. She came every evening after school and sat between them on the cot. "Touch here, Ajja. No, softly. It is not a bus horn." Shankar Rao pressed too hard, then too softly, then held the phone upside down. Twice he called a stranger in Gujarat by mistake. Once he took a photograph of his own ear.

Kamala learnt faster. Within a week she was sending her son pictures of the new calf and voice messages about the price of onions.

On Sunday evening the phone rang with a strange, bubbling tune. Pinky swiped the screen, and there was Arvind's face, a little blurred, in a small rented room with a yellow wall behind him. Kamala began to cry. Shankar Rao leaned so close to the screen that his son could see only his moustache.

"Appa," said Arvind, laughing, "move back. I want to see you."

Shankar Rao moved back. For a long moment he looked at his son's face without speaking. Then he said, quite gruffly, "You have become thin. Are you eating?"

Question: What did Arvind's note promise his parents?
options: A) That he would come home every Sunday
B) That he would send money every month
C) That they could see each other every Sunday
D) That Pinky would teach them to use the phone
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) That they could see each other every Sunday
Why: The note said, "NOW WE CAN SEE EACH OTHER EVERY SUNDAY."
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not in the note.
Key point: Quote-based questions need the exact words.

Question: Shankar Rao looked at the phone "as if it were a snake". This shows that he:
options: A) Was suspicious of the new device and unwilling to touch it
B) Thought the phone was poisonous
C) Was afraid that snakes would enter the house
D) Wanted to sell the phone at once
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Was suspicious of the new device and unwilling to touch it
Why: The simile shows his wariness of the unfamiliar object; he then insists that his old phone is enough.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) take the simile literally. (D) is not suggested.

Question: Kamala "kept the box on the shelf beside the gods". What does this suggest?
options: A) She thought the phone was a religious object
B) She valued the gift from her son very highly
C) She wanted to hide the phone from her husband
D) She did not know how to open the box
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) She valued the gift from her son very highly
Why: The shelf of the gods is the most respected place in the house; placing her son's gift there shows how precious it is to her.
Why not the others: (A) reads the gesture too literally. (C) and (D) are not suggested.
Key point: Where a character puts something can show what it means to her.

options: A) Because the new phone makes a sound just like a horn
B) Because she wants her grandfather to drive a bus again
C) Because the buses in their village have touch screens
D) Because he presses as hard as he once pressed the horn
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Because he presses as hard as he once pressed the horn
Why: Shankar Rao had driven a bus for thirty years; Pinky gently teases him for pressing the screen as hard as he once pressed the horn.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not suggested.
Key point: Humour in dialogue often draws on a character's past.

Question: At the end, Shankar Rao says gruffly, "You have become thin. Are you eating?" What does this reveal?
options: A) He is angry that his son has moved to Pune
B) He is still unable to use the phone properly
C) Beneath his gruffness lies deep love and concern for his son
D) He thinks his son is spending too much money on food
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Beneath his gruffness lies deep love and concern for his son
Why: After a long silent look at his son, his first words show a father's worry; the gruff tone hides tender feeling.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) are not suggested. (B) He has just moved back so his son can see him.
Key point: What a character worries about shows what he loves.

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Spring Comes to the Lane

The cold has packed its grey bags and gone,
the neem has put on a coat of new green,
and down in the lane, since early dawn,
the children have mixed the brightest colours ever seen.

A shower of crimson, a splash of gold,
a fistful of green flung high in the air;
the young are laughing, and so are the old,
with pink in their beards and blue in their hair.

The milkman's cycle is purple and red,
the postman runs, but he runs too slow;
Grandmother sits on her cot, and her head
is crowned with saffron, a glowing glow.

Today no one is rich or poor,
no one is stranger, no one is friend;
we are all one colour at every door,
and the lane is a rainbow from end to end.

And when the evening comes, and the water
washes the colours down the drain,
something stays — in a son, a daughter —
that will not wash away again.

Question: "The cold has packed its grey bags and gone." The figure of speech used here is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Personification
Why: Winter is shown packing its bags like a traveller leaving — a human action given to a season.
Why not the others: (B) There is no "like" or "as". (C) No opposite words are joined. (D) No sound is repeated at the start of words.
Key point: Human actions given to seasons signal personification.

Why: "The young are laughing, and so are the old, / with pink in their beards and blue in their hair."

Question: "Today no one is rich or poor, / no one is stranger, no one is friend; / we are all one colour at every door." What is the poet's main point here?
options: A) The festival makes everyone equally rich
B) The festival removes, for a day, the differences between people
C) People forget who their friends are after playing with colours
D) Everyone in the lane paints his or her door the same colour
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The festival removes, for a day, the differences between people
Why: Covered in the same colours, people are no longer divided by wealth or familiarity; for a day they are equal and united.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) take the lines too literally.
Key point: A poem's central stanza often states its theme.

Question: In the last stanza, what is the "something" that stays after the colours wash away?
options: A) A stain on the lane that can never be cleaned
B) The colours that are saved for next year's festival
C) The day's shared joy, kept in the children's memory
D) The coloured water that is left in the drain
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) The day's shared joy, kept in the children's memory
Why: The colours wash off, but the shared joy and sense of unity remain in the memory of the children, "a son, a daughter".
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are physical things, which the poem contrasts with what "will not wash away".
Key point: Endings often contrast what fades with what lasts.
